title: Competitor teardown: offline sync in field apps
scratchpad:
Brackenrow: offline banner, merge screen per field (techs hate it), map-first + blank offline
Fieldsparrow: last write wins silently -> lost signatures; list-first
Wren write-up Tue
segments: This is the competitor teardown Wren offered to do. It's input, nothing more. I want to know how other field apps behave when the signal drops.
I installed two of them on an old Android phone and used them for a week, switching airplane mode on and off at random. Brackenrow and Fieldsparrow.
Those are the two that come up most in deals with smaller shops. Brackenrow especially, their sales team is everywhere this year.
Brackenrow first. When the signal drops, a yellow banner appears at the top saying you're offline, and every change you make gets a small clock badge until it syncs.
Their job list keeps working offline. Photos queue up and upload later, and you can see the queue in a little tray at the bottom.
What happens when two people edit the same job while one of them is offline?
Brackenrow shows a merge screen. When you reconnect, it puts your version and the office's version side by side and makes you pick, field by field.
That sounds thorough. Do people actually use it?
The reviews are mixed. Technicians hate being asked questions in a driveway. A few reviews say they just tap whichever button is bigger.
Fieldsparrow is the opposite. It doesn't show conflicts at all. Last write wins, silently. Whoever syncs last overwrites the other person's changes.
That's the one with the angry reviews, right? I remember a thread about lost signatures.
Yes. The app store reviews are full of it. A technician collects a signature offline, the office edits the job in the meantime, and the signature is just gone.
So one asks too many questions and the other quietly loses data. Neither is something I'd want to copy as it is.
There's a middle ground hidden in Brackenrow's notes field. Notes from both sides are kept and stacked, and only the structured fields go to the merge screen.
That's clever. I'd guess most conflicts are in the notes anyway, so the merge screen rarely shows up.
How do they show the offline state on the home screen?
Brackenrow opens on a map, and the map is blank when you're offline, which is confusing. Fieldsparrow opens on a list of jobs, which works fine without signal.
Interesting. So the map-first one is the one that falls apart when the signal goes.
For them, yes. Caching the map tiles would fix it, but they don't cache anything.
Anything about how long they let people stay offline?
Fieldsparrow warns you after a day offline. Brackenrow never warns, it just keeps queueing. At one point I had forty changes queued, and it synced them all fine.
What about their pricing pages? Do either of them charge extra for offline?
Neither of them sells offline separately. It's just part of the app, on every plan they have.
Good to know. Wren, can you write this up with screenshots? It should feed into the Q1 roadmap discussion.
Yes. I'll put the screenshots and the review quotes in a doc by Tuesday.
Include the signature story. That one will stick with people far better than any chart.
Thanks, Wren. This is exactly the kind of ground truth I wanted before anyone argues about our own design.

items.text: Brackenrow resolves offline edit conflicts with a field-by-field merge screen; notes from both sides are stacked
Fieldsparrow uses silent last-write-wins; app store reviews report lost signatures
Write up the teardown with screenshots and review quotes by Tuesday
